name: Castles and Town Walls of King Edward in Gwynedd
countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
description: Along the coast of north Wales stand four mighty fortresses, Beaumaris, Harlech, Caernarfon and Conwy, raised by Edward I after he conquered the Welsh princes in 1282. Conwy and Caernarfon are still hemmed in by their medieval town walls, and Harlech perches on a crag above the sea. Together they form the so-called Ring of Iron, among Europe's best-preserved medieval strongholds.
